title: High Viscosity / Mix Too Hard
shortDescription: Freezing cylinder torque exceeds safe limit — mix frozen too hard.
fullDescription:
Taylor soft-serve machines (the famously broken McDonald's C602, C709, C708, C713) monitor beater motor torque as a proxy for mix viscosity. E1 trips when the mix is frozen too hard — the beater cannot turn safely and the machine locks out to protect the drive belt and gearbox.

This is the infamous McDonald's ice cream machine fault that spawned internet fame and led to the Kytch lawsuit. The machine is designed such that only a certified McDonald's or Taylor technician can clear certain faults, which is why the machines appear 'always broken' to customers. The real root cause is usually a heat-mode calibration issue — the nightly heat cycle did not complete because the machine was opened, or the mix level dropped below the low probe during heat cycle, causing the machine to reject the cycle and enter a diagnostic state only a tech can clear.

causes.cause: Mix level too low during heat cycle

symptoms: Very hard product if it dispenses at all

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn main switch off for 5 minutes; restore power. Many E1 faults clear with this but may recur.

fixSteps.title: Verify mix level
fixSteps.instruction: Top off both hoppers with fresh mix to above the low-level probes before any heat cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect scraper blades
fixSteps.instruction: On next brush clean, confirm scraper blades installed per Taylor manual (beveled edge leading).

fixSteps.title: Call Taylor service
fixSteps.instruction: If E1 returns after power cycle, Taylor or authorized technician must enter service menu to clear fault history and recalibrate viscosity.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — Taylor service menus require a technician passcode per McDonald's contract.
videoSearchQuery: McDonalds Taylor C602 E1 viscosity fix

faq.q: Why is the McDonald's ice cream machine always broken?
faq.a: Most 'broken' machines are in the nightly 4-hour heat-mode pasteurization cycle, or are locked out on E1/E2 after a heat cycle aborted. Real hardware failures are less common than perception suggests.
Power cycling sometimes works. Persistent E1 requires Taylor technician access to the service menu.
A third-party device that tried to expose these diagnostics to operators; Taylor and McDonald's pushed back, leading to ongoing litigation.

title: Heat Mode / Pasteurization Cycle Failed
shortDescription: Nightly heat-mode pasteurization cycle did not complete within required time/temp parameters.
fullDescription:
Taylor machines in health-code heat-treat jurisdictions run a nightly 4-hour pasteurization cycle heating mix to 151F (66C) to pasteurize, then cooling back to 41F (5C). E2 means that cycle failed — typically because mix level dropped below the low probe, the door was opened, power was interrupted, or the heater/probe failed to reach target temperature.

The machine locks out until a certified technician clears E2 and restarts the heat cycle. This is the other half of the 'McDonald's ice cream is broken' phenomenon — crews open the machine during the cycle to check it, which aborts the cycle and causes E2.

causes.cause: Heat cycle interrupted (door opened / power blip)
Mix level dropped below probe during cycle

symptoms: All product must be discarded per health code

fixSteps.title: Discard product
fixSteps.instruction: Per health code, any mix that failed heat cycle must be discarded.

fixSteps.title: Refill with fresh mix
fixSteps.instruction: Refill hoppers to full mark with fresh mix.

fixSteps.title: Tech must clear and restart
fixSteps.instruction: Taylor technician clears E2 via service menu and restarts 4-hour heat cycle — machine is offline until complete.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — E2 is a health-code food-safety fault and must be cleared by a technician.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor C602 E2 heat mode fail

faq.a: No — most US jurisdictions require nightly heat pasteurization for dairy-based soft serve.

faq.q: Why does opening the door break it?
faq.a: Opening breaks the sealed pasteurization — machine cannot validate temperature was held.

title: Beater Motor Overload
shortDescription: Beater motor drew over-current — stalled or bound.
fullDescription:
E3 is a hard motor overload — the beater that scrapes the freezing cylinder is drawing more current than the motor starter allows. Usually related to E1 (viscosity) but more severe — the machine tripped the starter, not just the soft viscosity alarm.

Causes: frozen-solid mix in cylinder, broken drive belt, scraper blade jammed.

causes.cause: Drive belt broken or slipped off

fixSteps.title: Reset motor starter
fixSteps.instruction: Locate motor overload reset button on side of starter inside panel; press.

fixSteps.title: Technician service
fixSteps.instruction: If overload trips again, tech must disassemble for cylinder inspection.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — 208V three-phase motor work.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor soft serve E3 beater overload

faq.a: No — you will snap the drive shaft.

title: Hopper Temperature Too High
shortDescription: Mix hopper temperature exceeded safe holding threshold (typically 41F).
fullDescription:
Hopper holding temperature must stay at 33-41F per health code. E4 indicates temperature has risen above this threshold — usually because the hopper refrigeration compressor or fan failed, or product was added at warm temperature.

All mix must be discarded after an E4 event and machine service is required.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Crew cleans condenser daily per Taylor PM schedule.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — sealed system work EPA regulated.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor C602 E4 hopper temp high

faq.a: If above 41F for 4+ hours — yes, per FDA Food Code.

title: Draw Handle Switch Fault
shortDescription: Draw-handle switch inconsistent with expected state.
fullDescription: The draw handle operates a switch so the machine knows when to command the beater and advance the timer. E5 fires when the switch reports closed without the handle being pulled (stuck magnet, failed reed switch).
symptoms: Machine thinks handle is always pulled

fixSteps.title: Inspect handle magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Open door panel, ensure magnet is in handle.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor draw handle E5 reed switch

faq.a: Temporarily yes — proper repair uses OEM handle.

title: Freezing Cylinder Probe Fault
shortDescription: Cylinder temperature probe open or shorted.
fullDescription: E6 identifies failure of the freezing-cylinder temperature probe used for viscosity feedback. Without it, viscosity cannot be controlled. Often caused by damaged wire at the mechanical seal area.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Probe replacement requires freezing cylinder access.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

title: Compressor Fault — Cylinder Refrigeration
shortDescription: Freezing cylinder compressor failed to start or tripped overload.
fullDescription: E7 applies to the cylinder-side compressor. Repeated restart failures cause lockout. Usually dirty condenser, failed start components, or mechanical compressor issues.
whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor soft serve E7 compressor fault

faq.a: Yes — it's the #1 service call cause on Taylor machines.

title: Mix Low in Hopper
shortDescription: Hopper mix level below low-level probe.
fullDescription: E8 is an alert not a full fault — tells staff to refill the hopper. Critical during heat-mode cycle because it will abort the cycle and cause E2.

fixSteps.title: Refill hopper
fixSteps.instruction: Add fresh pre-chilled mix to fill line.

faq.q: Can I top off during service?
faq.a: Yes — during normal serve. Never during heat cycle.

title: Hopper Probe Fault
fullDescription: E9 indicates the hopper probe is open or shorted. Without it the controller cannot verify hopper temperature during heat cycle — safety-critical, so machine locks out.
whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Heat cycle validates temperature to pasteurize — can't do that blind.

title: Power Fail During Heat Cycle
fullDescription: E10 specifically flags a power-interrupted heat cycle. Because temperature hold cannot be validated, the machine demands disposal of mix and a full restart of the 4-hour heat cycle by a technician.

fixSteps.title: Discard mix
fixSteps.instruction: Per food code, discard all mix in hoppers and cylinders.

fixSteps.title: Refill and restart cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Tech clears E10 and restarts 4-hour heat cycle — machine offline all day.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.
videoSearchQuery: Taylor C602 E10 power fail heat cycle

faq.a: The machine draws too much current for a standard UPS; a dedicated circuit with surge protection helps.

title: Brush-Clean Reminder
shortDescription: Scheduled brush-cleaning interval reached (typically every 14 days).
fullDescription: Taylor heat-treat machines require a full manual brush-clean every 14 days. CLEAN reminder prompts disassembly, sanitizing of all parts, and reassembly — typically a 90-minute process. Skipping it causes product quality and ultimately E1/E2 faults.

fixSteps.title: Follow Taylor brush-clean SOP
fixSteps.instruction: Drain, disassemble, brush-clean all parts with Stera-Sheen or equivalent, sanitize, reassemble, lubricate o-rings.

whenToCallPro: Normally crew task; pro if O-rings need replacing.

faq.a: Health inspectors cite for missed brush cleans; it's mandatory.

title: Heat Mode Cycle In Progress
shortDescription: Nightly 4-hour heat-mode pasteurization in progress — machine unavailable.
fullDescription:
HEAT MODE is not a fault but an indication the machine is in its 4-hour pasteurization cycle. Mix is heated to 151F held, then cooled back to hopper temperature. During this time the machine cannot dispense. Any interruption throws E2 or E10.

This is the real answer to 'Why is the McDonald's ice cream machine always broken?' — it's often just in heat mode, and crew schedules mean it's sometimes running during customer hours.

fixSteps.title: Wait for cycle completion
fixSteps.instruction: Do not open any door. Wait up to 4 hours for cycle to finish.

fixSteps.title: Schedule overnight
fixSteps.instruction: Start heat mode at close so it finishes before open.

videoSearchQuery: Taylor soft serve heat mode cycle how long

faq.a: Approximately 4 hours — heat up, hold, cool down.

faq.q: Why can't I use the machine?
faq.a: Product is above freeze temp during pasteurization.
